newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn group objects to proposed wetland rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn group objects to proposed wetland rules.

text.p: Proposed wetland conservation regulations in the new U.S. farm bill stray too far from the original intent of legislation and would require major changes from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the National Corn Growers Association said in a news release on Friday.
"The proposed rules, especially those dealing with wetlands, must be revised before farmers find them acceptable," said Wallie Hardie, North Dakota farmer and president of the NGCA, in the release.
The corn group was reacting to proposed new rules and comments submitted to USDA as part of the department's initial action to carry out the conservation title of the farm bill.
The provision that called for certification of existing wetland determination will cause corn farmers the most problems.
"Farmers have already been through this," Hardie said. "There is no good reason to force us to revisit wetland determinations."
